items_missed: 1_set_agenda: never asked the customer's name, never asked 'how are you today,' gave no real agenda statement (what he'd cover + rough time), never got an explicit 'sound good?'

2_probe: no address/zip for origin or destination, no stairs check at the origin house, no question on additional rooms (garage/storage), no packing-services question, no storage-stop question, no additional-stops question, no 'anything you're worried about' stressor question

3_pricing: no 'pricing is super simple' opener, never listed what's included (gas, truck, insurance, wrap pads, tools), no disassembly/reassembly mention despite the move being beds and bedroom sets, no packing-service pricing, No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned, Meet Your Mover never mentioned, On-Time Guarantee never mentioned, no full no-hidden-fees pitch (credit card/fuel surcharge/assembly fees)
4_clock: never said the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, no sense-check ('does that make sense?') after explaining the minimum/proration

5_estimate: customer directly asked 'are you thinking two people or is that enough?' and Sergio moved on to the booking date without ever answering; no assembly/disassembly variable called out even though beds were the main item
6_save_your_ass: skipped entirely — no prep-before-move-day pitch, no consolidation examples, no carload tip, no close
7_quote_booking: never said 'no deposit required,' never mentioned the bolded summary at the top of the confirmation email, never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?'
8_politeness: never obtained or used the customer's name at any point on the call, so the 3+ name-use bullet is a hard miss
9_bonus: no rapport-building or humor beyond casual affirmations, no insurance explanation (No Worries coverage / 60 cents per lb) at all
top_strength: Sergio ran a tight, efficient 5-minute call and gave a clear, tailored estimate ('I would probably keep this around that three and a half to four and a half hour range... a cost between $700 to $900') plus offered a same-day lock-in on the spot ('Did you want to lock that in or did you want to receive the quote and think it through?').
coaching_note: You never got the caller's name, which killed the politeness score and made the whole call feel transactional — always ask and use it. When she asked directly 'are you thinking two people or is that enough,' you talked past it into the booking date instead of answering; always close the loop on a direct question before moving on. Biggest gap: you skipped every differentiator (No Worries coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee) and the whole Save Your Ass prep speech because the move felt small and simple — those are exactly the things that protect the bill and set expectations, so they need to be in every call regardless of size.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and casually warm throughout ('Awesome,' 'Cool,' 'No worries'), but stayed transactional, never used the customer's name, and let her direct question about crew size go unanswered.
